notebook.name: changeset
notebook.title: Read a changeset
notebook.description: Read one of the notebook's changesets by the id log gives: its kind, client, author, times, message, counts, what it reverts and what reverted it, and whether it renames or moves nodes; then what it did to each node it changed, a page at a time by node id: where the node was before and after in the tree, the revision of the content it wrote, and the node's current path (null when it is in the trash or gone). The changeset itself comes on the first page, without cursor; go on with next_cursor while it is set. A changeset of another notebook is not found here. History is read-only here: people revert changesets in the web.

id.description: The changeset's id, as log gives it.

limit.description: At most this many changes, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: delete
notebook.title: Delete a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Put a page or an attachment in the notebook's trash, by its path from the notebook's root: people restore it from the trash in the web. A page with pages or attachments under it needs recursive set to true, which puts them in the trash with it. Any of its pages being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the deletion, saying by whom; the locks cannot be taken over. The answer has how many pages and attachments went to the trash, itself counted, and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The path of the page or attachment to delete, from the notebook's root.

recursive.description: Delete a page with its children, its pages and attachments. Default false: a page with children is refused.

notebook.name: edit
notebook.title: Edit a page
notebook.description: Replace old_string with new_string in a page's content on the server, byte for byte, as a find and replace: old_string must occur exactly once (occurrences that overlap count), unless replace_all is set, which replaces each, left to right. Copy old_string from what read gave, with enough of the text around it to be unique: quotes and spaces are matched as they are. On a page whose line breaks are all CRLF and an old_string without CR, old_string's bare LFs are matched as CRLF and new_string's are written as CRLF (a CR in new_string stays); with a CR in old_string, both are taken as given. Without base_version, the edit applies to the content as it is now, made once more if the page changed while it was made; with base_version, it is refused when the page changed since. A page being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the edit, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the page's version, how many times old_string was replaced, changed (false when the content stayed as it was), and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md": its ancestors' titles, then its own title and ".md".

old_string.description: The text to replace, copied from what read gave, byte for byte: 1 byte to 1 MiB.

new_string.description: The text to put in its place, which differs from old_string.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of old_string, left to right. Default false: old_string must occur exactly once.

base_version.description: The page's version, as read, list or write gave it: the edit is refused when the page changed since. Without it, the edit applies to the content as it is now.

notebook.name: list
notebook.title: List nodes
notebook.description: List the notebook's pages and attachments. With pattern empty or "/", the root's children; with "A/B/", the children of the page A/B.md; both in the tree's order. Any other pattern is a glob over the paths, in path order: * matches within a segment, ? one character, ** any number of segments as a segment of its own ("**/*.md" is every page, "A/**" everything under A). Matching ignores case. Each item has its path, its kind (page or attachment) and whether it has children; a page also its version, size and last change, an attachment its type and size. An answer holds at most limit items and about 48 KiB, and a costly glob over a large notebook stops after a bounded amount of matching, maybe with no items: whenever next_cursor is set, pass it back as cursor to go on. A path without wildcards that names nothing may come with a hint, as when it names a page without its .md.

pattern.description: "" or "/" for the root's children, "A/B/" for the children of A/B.md, or a glob. Default: the root's children.

limit.description: At most this many items, 1 to 1000. Default 200.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: log
notebook.title: List the notebook's changes
notebook.description: List the notebook's changesets, newest first: what people and agents changed, each with its kind, client, author (id and display name), times, message, how many nodes and contents it changed, what it reverts and what reverted it, and its first three changes; a changeset too large for the answer comes alone, its changes cut to fit and changes_cut true. path keeps the changesets that changed that page or attachment; actor those of an account, "me" for yours; client those of a client, "mcp" for every agent. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. changeset reads one in full. History is read-only here: people restore versions and revert changesets in the web.

path.description: Only the changesets that changed the page or attachment at this path, from the notebook's root.

actor.description: Only the changesets by this account: its id, or "me" for yours.

client.description: Only the changesets of this client: "web", "api", "cli", "mcp:<name>" for an agent, or "mcp" for every agent.

limit.description: At most this many changesets, 1 to 100. Default 50.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: move
notebook.title: Move or rename a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Move, rename, or both at once, a page or an attachment: from is its path, to the full path it will have, both from the notebook's root ("Archive/Plan 2026.md"), never a page to move it into. A page's path ends with .md, and an attachment's keeps an extension, which may change. A page moves with its children. The page above to must exist: move creates no pages. The links to what moves, and to its pages, are rewritten to follow it, unless update_links is false, which leaves every page linking to it as it is: those links may then lead elsewhere, or nowhere. Rewriting the links of a page being edited in the web editor, by you too, is refused, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the new path, node_id, changed, and the changeset's id and time (null when nothing moved).

from.description: The path of the page or attachment to move, from the notebook's root.

to.description: The full path it will have, its new name last: never a page to move it into. The page above it must exist.

update_links.description: Rewrite the links to what moves, and to its pages, so that they follow it. Default true.

notebook.name: read
notebook.title: Read a page or an attachment
notebook.description: Read a page or an attachment by its path from the notebook's root; a page's path ends with .md. A page comes as two text blocks: a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored, frontmatter, byte order mark and CRLF included. offset is the first line, from 1; limit the number of lines, 2000 by default. An answer holds about 48 KiB at most, its metadata line included: go on from next_offset, and from next_column when a line was too long for one answer; the parts read in turn are the whole content. An attachment comes as its metadata (type, size, SHA-256, width and height, how to link it, a download address valid for an hour or two), then the image itself for a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP of at most 3 MiB and 8000 pixels a side, or else a link to download it. Without the server's public address set (server.public_url) there is no download address: an image still comes itself, any other attachment as its metadata only, with a note saying so.

path.description: The path from the notebook's root: "A/B.md" for a page, "A/diagram.png" for an attachment.

column.description: The byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: At most this many lines, from 1. Default 2000.

notebook.name: versions
notebook.title: List or read a page's versions
notebook.description: Without revision, list a page's versions, newest first: each with its revision, size, times, and the changeset that wrote it (its kind, client and author); the answer also has the page's current version. Go on with next_cursor while it is set. With revision, read that version's content as read reads a page: two text blocks, a line of JSON metadata (path, kind, revision, current_version, offset, column, lines, total_lines, byte_size, next_offset, next_column), then its lines exactly as stored; go on from next_offset, and next_column. The version answered has its own revision, which may be above the one asked for: an edit session's saves share one version. Revisions are for reading: write and edit take the page's version, from read. A page in the trash has no path: its versions are read in the web.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md".

revision.description: The revision to read, from 1. Without it, the list of the page's versions.

offset.description: With revision: the first line, from 1. Default 1.

column.description: With revision: the byte of the first line to start from, from 0: next_column of the previous answer. Default 0.

limit.description: Without revision: at most this many versions, 1 to 100, default 50. With revision: at most this many lines, from 1, default 2000.

cursor.description: Without revision: next_cursor of the previous answer, to go on from there.

notebook.name: write
notebook.title: Write a page
notebook.description: Write a page's whole content by its path from the notebook's root; the path ends with .md. Without base_version, it creates the page, and the parent pages it lacks, empty, in one change; a path that is a page already is refused. With base_version, the version read, list or write gave, it replaces the content of the page at the path: refused when the page changed since, or when the path names another page now; read it again. When the page holds that content already, nothing is written and changed is false, with an older base_version of that page too, and while the page is being edited. The content is stored byte for byte: at most 5 MiB of UTF-8, without NUL. A page being edited in the web editor, by you too, refuses the write, saying by whom; the lock cannot be taken over. The answer has the page's path, node_id and version, changed (false when nothing was written), the nodes it created, and the changeset's id and time.

path.description: The page's path from the notebook's root, as "A/B.md": its ancestors' titles, then its own title and ".md".

content.description: The page's whole content, as it will be stored: frontmatter, byte order mark and line breaks included.

base_version.description: The page's version, as read, list or write gave it, to replace its content. Without it, the page is created.

account.name: notebooks
account.title: List your notebooks
account.description: List the notebooks you can see in every workspace you belong to, each with its id, its name, its workspace's slug and name, and your role (admin, editor or reader), by workspace, then by name. Open one with open_notebook, then pass its id as notebook to the other tools. truncated is true when there were more than one answer holds.

account.name: open_notebook
account.title: Open a notebook
account.description: Open a notebook: its instructions for agents (its root page AGENTS without its frontmatter, or the server's built-in ones when it has none) and an overview: how many pages and attachments it holds, when it last changed (null when nothing was ever written in it), and the nodes at its root. Follow its instructions while you work in it, and pass its id as notebook to the other tools. truncated is true when the root's nodes were cut short.
